text:
jordan: Noticed a nasty client-visible error when we evict nodes during a hosted->private handoff. Requests get 502s for ~8s. Putting notes and possible fixes here before a proper RFC.

jordan: Root cause seems to be lease semantics: router holds a short-lived lease token for a connection but runtime expects a per-connection ephemeral session. When we reassign capacity the router drops routing immediately; runtime drains slowly and in-flight KV/streams lose mapping.

eric: Can you share the sequence? Is this only for streaming responses or also regular generation calls?

jordan: Both, but streaming makes it obvious. Sequence: 1) router marks node evicted and stops routing new requests 2) router revokes lease token 3) runtime still has active session + KV, but token mismatch triggers auth failure on next refresh -> immediate 502.

priya: Do we have a token refresh path that tolerates transient revocation? Current contract is strict: token must match handshake id.

jordan: Right now it's strict. We discussed soft-revoke before but didn't implement.

olivia: Soft-revoke sounds promising: mark token as draining for TTL and allow in-flight requests until TTL expiry. But risk: attacker could replay drained token? Need to scope to internal control plane tokens and tie to node identity.

eric: Another approach: graceful handoff where router toggles routing to "drain-only" and uses 0 new routing but continues to accept reconnects for a short window. Router would signal runtime withDrain=true during eviction API call.

priya: Implementation idea: add lease_v2 to manifest/control plane with fields: drain_ttl, allow_reconnects(bool), verify_node_id. Eg: ```
lease_v2:
  drain_ttl: 15s
  allow_reconnects: true
  verify_node_id: true
```

jordan: That would be a manifest-level opt-in for tenants; default keep old strict behaviour. For Private deployments default drain_ttl=5s for security reasons; hosted could default 30s.

olivia: We'll need runtime changes: accept tokens in states {active, draining} and treat draining tokens as valid for existing sessions + reconnections from same node_id. New sessions from other nodes should be rejected.

eric: Also add a short grace-window for streaming clients: if stream reconnects within drain_ttl and presents previous stream id, we reattach. Otherwise reject. That avoids app-visible broken streams.

priya: Tests: 1) evict-during-100rps streaming test, measure visible 502s 2) node compromise simulation: token reuse from different node_id should fail 3) private default TTL enforcement test.

jordan: Ops/Console changes: show lease_state per node (active/draining/revoked) and expose drains in rollout UI so SREs can see in-flight counts before eviction.

olivia: Metric ideas: lease_revoke_rate, lease_drain_reconnects, lease_auth_failures_post_revoke. Add histogram for drain duration.

eric: Backwards compatibility: router must negotiate lease_v2 handshake; if runtime doesn't support it, fall back to v1 strict revoke. We'll need a capability bit in the adapter handshake.

priya: Security note: for Private deployments with HSM-backed node identities we can tighten allow_reconnects=false. Document this as part of private deployment security guide.

jordan: Short-term mitigation: increase router drain grace to 15s for critical tenants while we prototype. Patch rolled to staging.

infra-bot: deploy-trigger: requested by jordan. Canary env: staging-lease-drain. Rolling 20% -> 100%. Logs to #eng-runtime.

olivia: For the RFC, include state machine diagram for token lifecycle: issued -> active -> draining -> revoked. Also include sequence diagrams for streaming reconnect.

eric: Also call out cost tradeoff: longer drain_ttl increases capacity holding and can hurt autoscaling responsiveness. Include an autoscaler safety limit param.

priya: I'll draft the tests and security appendix. jordan can write the sequence diagrams.

jordan: I'll open RFC by EOW. Will include sample manifest snippet, handshake proto change, runtime acceptance rules, and Console hooks.

olivia: Nice. Also note that Dedicated customers may want editable drain_ttl per pool via console. Add to requirements.

jordan: Thanks all.

infra-bot: canary-status: 20% complete, no increase in 5xx observed so far.
